translation_notes: prefixes: XSD->xsd; only xsd is declared (owl/rdf/rdfs/foaf of the draft never appear as prefixed names: RDF.type is `a`, the lab6 vocabulary is the instance attribute `self.lab6`, built at run time from `self.lab6_ns_str`, so it stays `{self.lab6.City}` interpolations).

the 9 `Literal(row[i], datatype=XSD.x)` calls become `{row[i]}^^xsd:x` (string x6, float x2, long x1), NOT `".."^^`: the cells are numpy / pandas values, and pandas gives a float64 column when it holds a NaN, so population reaches the island as 29617000.0 and the original makes "29617000.0"^^xsd:long (the driver pins this). `{expr}^^dt` goes through the same Literal(value, datatype=...) constructor, so the lexical forms agree; a mechanical "n"^^dt or f"{n}" would not be the same program for the float columns (rdflib normalises)

the graph is `self.g`, an attribute of the receiver: each island takes the call suffix `(self.g)` (`@graph self.g` is documented only for a bare name). one suffix per island (10 islands for the 13 adds), the cost of an attribute receiver.
`URIRef(entity_city_uri)` -> `f<{entity_city_uri}>` (no @base in scope, so identical; the name is already a full IRI, built with lab6_ns_str).

restructuring: the three adds at the top (city a City, city name_ascii, country a Country) are folded into ONE `+{ }` (one subject with `;`, a second subject after `.`); every other add keeps its own island because each sits under its own is_nan guard. Order of insertion is the only thing that changes (not observable in a graph).

driver: `self` is a stub with the attributes the region reads (the real Lab6Solution.__init__ reads a CSV with pandas and a DBpedia lookup; the lookup is not needed here), data read with the SAME pd.read_csv call; cities.csv has NaN cells in every guarded column, a Namibia 'NA' iso code that pandas reads as NaN, empty/other/admin/primary/minor capital values, rows skipped by the NaN guard, a country shared by two cities, names with space, comma and non-ASCII characters. The DataFrame is held as a class attribute of the per-call stub class because the harness compares instance __dict__s and a DataFrame has no usable ==.

anti-hollow-green: population via int(), float -> double, dropped datatype on iso2, an always-true guard on iso3, the country name triple removed, subject and object of the final triple swapped: rdfeval check FAILED each time; restored, green.

MISSING (minor): none for the coercion itself; the only cost is that the typed literal `^^` appears inside a one-triple island per guarded add, so the gain over `self.g.add((s, p, Literal(v, datatype=XSD.x)))` is the removal of the Literal/URIRef calls, not of the guards.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: entity_city_uri / entity_country_uri are built as URIRefs once, which removes the 13 `URIRef(...)` wrappers. The two type triples become one `self.g += [...]`. The nine column-to-literal adds become one loop over a table of (entity, prop, column, datatype), guarded by `if not self.is_nan(row[column])`; the original's section comments are kept inside the table. row[1] and row[4], the two unguarded adds, are non-NaN by the row-level `continue`, so the uniform guard is always true for them (is_nan is pure). The if/elif chain on row[8] becomes a dict `.get(row[8], self.lab6.cityIsLocatedIn)` (a NaN cell is hashable and falls to the default).

optimized.ldpy, written from optimized.py: `f<{self.lab6_ns_str}{row[…].lower().replace(" ", "_")}>` for the two entities (str + str, so the same as URIRef), one `+{ … a … . … a … }(self.g)` for the type triples, `xsd:` names in the table, and `+{ {entity} {prop} {row[column]}^^{datatype} }(self.g)` in the loop (interpolated datatype; same Literal(value, datatype=…) constructor, so the numpy float lexical forms agree).
No exception to the symmetry rule. Most of the gain is the rereading (the table loop), which leaves only one typed literal for the notation to compress.
header_optimization_notes: Python: BNode, OWL, RDFS and FOAF go. URIRef, Literal, RDF and XSD stay.
LD Python: both import lines go (nothing of rdflib is named in the region), and so do the owl:, rdf:, rdfs: and foaf: @prefix lines. Only xsd: stays.
